findings.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site that never set embed_category: in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, execute(...)[0]['id'] INNER JOINs site_settings on name = 'embed_category', but Discourse only writes site_settings rows for explicitly-changed settings, so in the default case the result set is empty, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate and blocking deploy/boot for most upgrading installs; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable, and line 15 has the same unguarded [0]['value'] pattern.

Migration inserts host values un-normalized, breaking previously-working embeds: raw strings like http://discourse.org are copied into host via SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison can never match referer host discourse.org; after upgrade, embeds on those sites fail with Discourse::InvalidAccess (invalid referer host) with no hint why, until an admin manually re-saves each host.

SQL string interpolation and blank-line junk rows in the migration INSERT: VALUES ('#{h}', ...) uses unvalidated free-text old setting values, so any value containing a single quote produces broken SQL and crashes the migration, and blank lines in the old setting insert host: '' rows that can never match anything.

Fabricator file contents are swapped: spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb received the old category_fabricator.rb content (all four :category fabricators) while spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines :embeddable_host; it only works because Fabrication loads by glob rather than filename, so anyone later editing the category fabricator edits the wrong file.

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController returns 500s instead of 404/422 on missing records/params: update/destroy do where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call methods on the result, so a stale id yields nil.host= / nil.destroy and a NoMethodError; params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises if the envelope is absent; and a nil host reaches before_validation where nil.sub! raises instead of producing a validation error.

Admin::EmbeddingController#update accepts a PUT and persists nothing: the action ignores the request body and just re-serializes, while the JS saveChanges action calls embedding.update({}); nothing in embedding.hbs invokes saveChanges today, but any future save button wired to it would silently discard user input while returning HTTP 200.

delete() in admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 swallows destroyRecord failures: destroyRecord().then(...) has no .catch, so if the DELETE fails the confirm dialog closes, the row remains, and no error is surfaced (unhandled rejection), unlike save() which correctly uses popupAjaxError.

Host validation vs. lookup mismatch on ports: the format regex in app/models/embeddable_host.rb explicitly permits a port ((:[0-9]{1,5})?), but record_for_host compares against uri.host which never includes a port, so a saved example.com:3000 authorizes nothing even though port-bearing entries worked under the old URI-parsed setting.
Host format regex requires a TLD (\.[a-z]{2,5}), so TLD-less hosts like localhost or intranet names — accepted by the old free-text setting — can no longer be created or re-saved through the UI.

_hydrateEmbedded plural branch in discourse/models/store.js.es6 crashes on any non-array *_ids value: now every key matching /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ is processed and obj[k].map(...) assumes an array, so a payload emitting foo_ids: null or a scalar throws inside shared hydration code, breaking find/findAll for that type entirely; also hydrated || [] is dead code and failed lookups insert nulls into the hydrated list.

Post-save client state diverges from the server in admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6: the buffer is never rolled back after a successful save, so re-editing shows the pre-normalization input (e.g. http://foo.com) while the row displays the server-normalized foo.com; and when the category chooser is cleared, the server saves uncategorized_category_id but the client sets category to findById(null) (undefined), so the badge renders blank until reload.

host.isSaving may not exist on RestModel: if RestModel (unlike Ember Data) does not define isSaving, the cantSave guard and the disabled=host.isSaving bindings are permanently falsy, and a double-click during a slow save issues two POSTs, creating duplicate host rows.

Store test asserts the wrong record: the pretender's /fruits/:id handler returns fruits[0], so store.find('fruit', 2) is served fruit 1 (apple), and the new plural-hydration assertions (colors length 2, ids 1 and 2) validate apple's color_ids rather than banana's [3]; the test passes for the wrong record and would not catch a lookup regression on the actually-requested record.

Embed hot path performance regression: `ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, issuing a DB query (`WHERE lower(host) = ?`) on every `/embed/comments` request, replacing the process-cached `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` which required zero DB traffic; the host list should be cached (process/Redis, invalidated on host CRUD) instead of queried per request

No functional index on `embeddable_hosts (lower(host))`: the table is created with only a PK, so the hot-path lookup `WHERE lower(host) = ?` cannot use a plain index and requires a sequential scan per embed request

Unbounded materialization in admin embedding endpoints: `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` loads and serializes every host row with no limit/pagination on every `show` and `update`; `update` additionally re-runs the full fetch+serialize while persisting nothing (frontend PUTs empty props)

Plural `*_ids` hydration in `store.js.es6` is O(ids × side-loaded records): the new plural branch maps each id through `_lookupSubType`, which linearly scans the side-loaded `root[pluralized]` array per id, causing quadratic-ish hydration for any future `embed: :ids` serializer with large arrays; an id→hash map should be built once per payload before hydrating

Migration crash: `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` in `create_embeddable_hosts.rb` raises NoMethodError when no `embed_category` row exists in `site_settings` (rows only exist for settings an admin has saved; default is `''`), so `db:migrate` crashes on any install that never configured embedding
Unsafe SQL interpolation in migration: the INSERT at line 24 of `create_embeddable_hosts.rb` interpolates `#{h}` into raw SQL, so a quote character in a legacy host line breaks the migration

Migration `create_embeddable_hosts` crashes with NoMethodError on any install where the `embed_category` setting was never changed from its default (no `site_settings` row exists), because `execute(...)[0]` returns nil and `nil['id']` is dereferenced — blocking every standard upgrade; masked in CI because test DBs are prepared from schema.rb so the data migration never runs

Migration copies embeddable host setting values verbatim via raw SQL without normalizing protocol/path (bypassing the model's `before_validation` stripping), so migrated rows like `http://discourse.org` or `example.com/1234` can never match the new exact `lower(host) = uri.host` lookup, silently breaking existing embeds and causing TopicRetriever to reject feeds after upgrade

`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` update/destroy raise 500 (NoMethodError) instead of 404 for unknown ids because `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil which is then dereferenced via `nil.host=`/`nil.destroy`
`save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without a presence check, causing a 500 on any request that omits the wrapper param
`EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` which crashes on a missing host value before validation can produce a 422

Store.js `_hydrateEmbedded` plural branch unconditionally deletes and replaces any payload attribute matching `*_ids` for every model, silently stripping non-association attributes ending in `_ids` from hydrated records, with no audit of other payloads shipping `*_ids` keys
Store.js plural hydration `obj[k].map(...)` throws TypeError if the `*_ids` value is null, a failure mode the singular branch did not have

Store.js plural hydration failed lookups produce arrays containing null entries (the `hydrated || []` fallback never applies since arrays are truthy), whereas the singular path preserved the raw id on failure

`EmbeddableHost` format validation advertises `host:port` support (regex permits `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but `record_for_host` compares against `URI(referer).host` which excludes the port, so a stored `example.com:3000` can never match and embeds from that host silently fail authorization

`PUT /admin/customize/embedding` update action re-renders `@embedding` without reading `params` at all, silently discarding any request body and returning 200 with no change — a no-op published API route

`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, `SiteSetting.embed_category`, and the class method `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` are removed outright with no deprecation path or alias, causing unknown-setting/NoMethodError failures for external consumers such as provisioning scripts, admin settings API clients, and plugins

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category lookup returns no rows: execute(...)[0] returns nil and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate on fresh installs and sites that never set embed_category; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable and would itself crash pre-seed

Migration copies old host values verbatim via raw INSERT, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so protocol-prefixed entries like http://discourse.org silently stop matching any referer after upgrade, causing the embed endpoint to reject previously-working hosts with InvalidAccess

update/destroy in admin/embeddable_hosts_controller crash with a 500 on a stale or missing host id: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil and is then used without a nil guard, reachable from the normal UI via concurrent edits or a double-click on delete

Client delete path in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch on destroyRecord(), so failed DELETE requests (network blip, 500, session expiry) reject unhandled with no message shown and the row stays in the table

Rolling back the migration permanently destroys the host whitelist: destructive, non-reversible data operations (INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts, DELETE FROM site_settings) live inside def change, so the table is dropped while the original setting rows are already deleted

PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op: the update action ignores the request body entirely and just re-serializes current state, and the client's saveChanges() calls embedding.update({}) with no error handling, so anything wired to this endpoint will succeed while persisting nothing

Malformed requests produce 500s instead of 422s: params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises NoMethodError when the embeddable_host key is absent, and self.host.sub!(...) in before_validation raises on a nil host before the format validation can produce a proper render_json_error response

No FK/index on embeddable_hosts.category_id and nothing cleans up when a category is deleted, leaving dangling category ids that render a blank category in the admin table and cause TopicEmbed.import to pass a nonexistent category id into PostCreator on the feed-polling job path

New plural hydration in store.js.es6 runs delete obj[k] unconditionally and assigns lookup results even when _lookupSubType returns undefined, so any *_ids payload whose records aren't side-loaded yields an array containing undefined and permanently loses the original id list
Unescaped SQL interpolation in the migration INSERT (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)) breaks the INSERT and aborts the migration when the old freeform setting value contains a single quote
Dotless hosts like localhost are now rejected by the host validation regex requiring a \.[a-z]{2,5} TLD segment, regressing dev/internal embedding setups that the old matcher supported

Admin controller specs (embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb, embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert Controller < Admin::AdminController - a static fact that cannot fail - leaving the feature's entire server write path untested: create/update/destroy, the blank category_id -> uncategorized defaulting, the render_json_error path on invalid hosts, and the param-nesting contract between the JS rest adapter and params[:embeddable_host]
update/destroy with a nonexistent id call save_host(nil) / nil.destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController, causing reachable 500s
A request missing the :embeddable_host param raises on nil[:host] in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController (line 25)

The expandable_first_post? test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes for the wrong reasons: it runs outside the nested describe's before hook so embed_truncate is still false and has_topic_embed? is not stubbed, while the actual behavioral change - a topic with an embed and embed_truncate enabled returns true even with zero hosts configured, since the embeddable_hosts.present? guard was removed from topic.rb - has no test; the test name describes a condition the code no longer checks

No integration/contract test for the serializer <-> store hydration chain: nothing verifies GET /admin/customize/embedding returns a payload the frontend store can hydrate (embed :ids producing embeddable_host_ids plus side-loaded records, the plural _hydrateEmbedded branch, pluralize('embeddable_host')); the only plural-hydration tests use the synthetic fruit/color fixture
EmbeddingController#update is a server-side no-op - it serializes without applying anything - yet the frontend saveChanges calls into it

The migration's embed_category lookup does execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i with no row-existence guard (unlike the guarded embeddable_hosts lookup), so a site without that row crashes the migration with NoMethodError
The migration's INSERT uses string interpolation, breaking on any host containing a quote
The migration's DELETE FROM site_settings inside change is irreversible on rollback - permanent data loss
The migration's data-transfer logic (embed_category lookup, host INSERT, site_settings DELETE) has no specs

The store test calls store.find('fruit', 2) (banana) but the pretender's /fruits/:id handler unconditionally returns fruits[0] (apple), so the assertions describe apple rather than the requested record - a mock-coupled test that validates the fixture and breaks the moment the mock is fixed to honor :id

EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's where("lower(host) = ?", host) lowercases only the stored column, not the input, so an uppercase referer host (e.g. EVILTROUT.COM) is denied despite the intent of case-insensitive matching; no spec covers this
EmbeddableHost's validation regex permits ports (:[0-9]{1,5}) but URI#host strips the port, so a stored example.com:8080 can never match any referer; no spec covers this

No negative-path validation tests for EmbeddableHost: the model spec only covers the three happy-path trims, with no assertion that an invalid host (e.g. 'not a host!') fails validation - which the controller's render_json_error path depends on - and record_for_host with nil/garbage input (fed via request.referer) is untested

The new admin frontend logic - the embeddable-host component's buffered rollback on cancel, dropping unsaved records on cancel, category_id propagation on save, and deleteHost bubbling, plus the admin-embedding controller - has no JS tests

The unmatched-host branch of TopicEmbed.import is untested: when the URL's host isn't configured, eh.try(:category_id) is nil and the topic lands in uncategorized - a behavior change from SiteSetting.embed_category with no test
TopicRetriever#invalid_host? was switched to the new embeddable-host gate with no corresponding spec

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the legacy `embed_category` setting was never saved: `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb dereferences the first row unconditionally, but site_settings only holds rows for settings changed from default, so fresh installs and sites that never set embed_category (or stored a category id instead of the category name the join assumes) get zero rows and db:migrate aborts

Migrated embed hosts are not normalized, so previously-working embed hosts silently stop matching: the migration inserts legacy values verbatim (e.g. `http://discourse.org`, `https://example.com/1234`), but the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches `lower(host) = uri.host` exactly, so any migrated entry carrying a scheme or path can never match again and embeds from those hosts break silently after upgrade
Unescaped string interpolation `#{h}` in the migration INSERT: a quote character in a legacy embeddable hosts value breaks the INSERT statement

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController returns 500s on unknown ids and missing params: update/destroy do `where(id: params[:id]).first` then call `save_host(nil)` / `nil.destroy` causing NoMethodError, and `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises when the embeddable_host key is absent; unknown ids should 404 and missing params should 422

`before_validation` in EmbeddableHost crashes on nil host: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil (e.g. an API create/update omitting host), turning what should be a 422 from validates_format_of into a 500

Fabricator files have swapped contents: the `:embeddable_host` fabricator lives in category_fabricator.rb and all four category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb; it only works because the directory is glob-loaded, and the name/content mismatch will misdirect anyone editing or grepping for category factories

The 'embedding' resource is a fake model with a dead write path: the update action persists nothing (it re-renders state rebuilt by fetch_embedding), nothing in embedding.hbs ever triggers the JS saveChanges action that calls it, and the 'model' is an OpenStruct with hardcoded id 'default' dressed up as a REST resource; a PUT endpoint that silently no-ops is a trap for future callers

ADMIN_MODELS string-munging (`type.replace('_', '-')` in rest.js.es6) papers over two type names for one model: `createRecord('embeddable-host')` (dashed) vs records hydrated from `embeddable_host_ids` keys (underscored), and the base adapter now hardcodes knowledge of a specific admin model; normalize the type once at the store boundary or give embeddable-host its own adapter overriding basePath

_hydrateEmbedded plural branch in store.js.es6 has dead code and unguarded failures: `hydrated || []` can never trigger since .map always returns a truthy array, failed lookups leave `false` entries in the hydrated array (the singular branch guards with `if (hydrated)` but the plural doesn't), and unconditional `delete obj[k]` destroys the raw ids of any pre-existing payload attribute ending in `_ids` that isn't a side-loaded association

The 'blank category → uncategorized' policy lives in the controller instead of the model: it is domain policy (the table enforces category_id NOT NULL) implemented in one controller action, so every other creation path (console, seeds, future jobs) must re-implement it or hit a DB error; move it to a before_validation on EmbeddableHost

Redundant serializer methods: `def id` / `def host` / `def category_id` in EmbeddableHostSerializer and EmbeddingSerializer merely restate what `attributes` already serializes — dead code implying customization where there is none
`create_table ... force: true` in the migration silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table (e.g. environments that ran an earlier iteration of the branch); migrations shouldn't force-drop

The EmbeddableHost validation regex advertises ports and paths that normalization/matching make unusable: before_validation strips paths before the format check so the regex's `(\/.*)?` branch is unreachable, and the regex allows ports but record_for_host compares against port-stripped `uri.host`, so a host saved as example.com:8080 validates, persists, and can then never match a referer

The embeddable-host component hand-syncs the category relation after save: `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId))` duplicates the server's relationship handling client-side, so a new host saved with a blank category (server assigns uncategorized, client sets undefined) renders with an empty category cell until reload; let the save response drive the update

Access-control rules disagree between layers: routes gate on AdminConstraint (admin-only) while controllers gate on ensure_staff (admin or moderator), and Admin::AdminController already applies its own auth filters; pick one privilege level and one layer

`record_for_host` returns false instead of nil on failure: a finder returning `record | false` is a type-boundary wart, and callers end up relying on quirks like `false.try(:category_id)` working (topic_embed.rb import); return nil so nil-safe idioms behave uniformly

New controller behavior is untested: both controller specs only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController`, a static fact, leaving the actual new logic (param handling, uncategorized defaulting, error rendering, 404s) with no coverage

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category setting row is absent (fresh installs and any site that never customized the default): the unguarded `[0]['id'].to_i` on an empty PG::Result at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11 raises nil['id'], aborting db:migrate and blocking deploys; it also crashes when the configured category was renamed/deleted since the join on s.value = c.name misses

Backfill copies host strings verbatim, bypassing the model's normalization: entries like `http://discourse.org` that previously worked (the old matcher stripped http(s):// at compare time) are stored as-is, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host never matches them and embeds from those hosts silently break with InvalidAccess; the backfill must apply the same sub! normalization or insert through the model

Irreversible destructive DELETE of the source settings inside `def change`: the raw `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` is not inverted on rollback, so rolling back drops the new table while the original settings are permanently gone with no recovery except backups; data migration belongs in `up` with a `down` that restores

SQL built via string interpolation with unescaped host values at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25: a stored entry containing a quote breaks the INSERT (migration fails mid-run after create_table) and is a SQL-injection vector from persisted setting data; use connection.quote or AR records

The uncategorized_category_id fallback is dead code and repeats the same crash pattern: `if category_id == 0` is unreachable because PG serial PKs start at 1 and the setting-absent case raises at line 11 rather than yielding 0, and the fallback itself uses the same unguarded `[0]['value']` so a minimal fix to the crash just moves it here

category_id is NOT NULL with no default, no FK, and no existence validation: the controller only defaults blank category ids so a nonexistent id saves silently, and deleting a category leaves embeddable_hosts.category_id dangling; that dangling id is passed to PostCreator with skip_validations: true, producing embedded topics pointing at a missing category
`create_table ... force: true` in a migration silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table — destructive DDL that also masks partial-failure states on re-runs

Fabricator file contents are swapped: the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb is byte-identical to the old category_fabricator.rb (defining all the :category fabricators) while category_fabricator.rb now defines :embeddable_host; it works only because fabrication loads by glob, and the placement will confuse future edits

Admin host controller 500s on nil record / malformed params: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is used immediately (save_host, host.destroy) causing NoMethodError on stale ids, and `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is read unguarded so a nil host crashes the model's `self.host.sub!` in before_validation before any clean validation error

Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that reports success: the PUT endpoint re-renders the serializer without applying anything, so any client saving embedding settings gets a 200 while the payload is dropped (the matching saveChanges frontend action is equally dead)

Migration crashes with NoMethodError on any database where `embed_category` was never set (fresh installs and most existing sites): `execute` returns a raw PG::Result, so when the site_settings query matches zero rows, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises, making `db:migrate` fail 100% of the time on a brand-new database; the `if category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable dead code

Migration inserts legacy host values verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` protocol stripping, so protocol-prefixed hosts like `http://discourse.org` can never match the exact-match `lower(host) = uri.host` lookup — embedding and feed polling silently stop working after upgrade; the migration then DELETEs the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting rows, destroying the admin's only copy of the data, and blank lines from the old setting get inserted as empty-string hosts

`Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a silent-pass endpoint: it never reads params and never mutates anything (byte-for-byte identical to `show`), returning 200 with a serialized 'updated' object while discarding all submitted changes, and the frontend already has a `saveChanges` action pointed at it

`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` update and destroy do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no presence check, so unknown ids cause `nil.host =` / `nil.destroy` NoMethodError 500s instead of 404/422 (e.g., a stale UI row after another admin deletes the host), and `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises when the nested param is absent or not a hash

Dangling `category_id` references: `EmbeddableHost` has no `dependent:` option, FK, or validation, so deleting a category leaves hosts pointing at a dead category — `TopicEmbed.import` passes the dead `category_id` to `PostCreator` causing silent embedded-topic creation failures, the admin UI renders a blank category badge, and `edit()` reading `host.category.id` → undefined means the next save sends no `category_id` and silently reassigns the host to uncategorized
`before_validation` crashes on nil host: `self.host.sub!` on nil raises NoMethodError, so a create/update request missing the `host` key gets a 500 instead of a 422 with a useful validation message

Hosts with ports validate but can never match anything: the host regex explicitly allows `example.com:3000`, but `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` which excludes the port, leaving silently dead configuration with no indication why embedding is denied

Store hydration plural branch has different and more dangerous failure semantics than the singular branch: it unconditionally deletes the original `*_id` key, assigns a junk pluralized key, and calls `.map` with no array check — silently stripping any pre-existing non-side-loadable `*_ids` attribute from client records site-wide, and throwing on null/non-array values to kill hydration of the whole payload

Post-save category state diverges from the server when no category was chosen: for a new host saved without touching the chooser, `categoryId` is null and the backend defaults to uncategorized, but the frontend sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` → undefined, so the row renders with no category badge until reload

Migration robustness: the INSERT interpolates legacy host strings directly into SQL (a single quote in a legacy value aborts the migration), `create_table ... force: true` silently drops any pre-existing table, and the `DELETE FROM site_settings` has no down-migration so `db:rollback` permanently destroys the legacy `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` values with no recovery
`destroyRecord()` has no failure handler: a failed DELETE produces an unhandled rejection with no error surfaced and the row just stays, unlike `save` which uses `popupAjaxError`

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site that never set embed_category: in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, execute(...)[0]['id'] INNER JOINs site_settings on name = 'embed_category', but Discourse only writes site_settings rows for explicitly-changed settings, so in the default case the result set is empty, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate and blocking deploy/boot for most upgrading installs; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable, and line 15 has the same unguarded [0]['value'] pattern.

Migration inserts host values un-normalized, breaking previously-working embeds: raw strings like http://discourse.org are copied into host via SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison can never match referer host discourse.org; after upgrade, embeds on those sites fail with Discourse::InvalidAccess (invalid referer host) with no hint why, until an admin manually re-saves each host.

SQL string interpolation and blank-line junk rows in the migration INSERT: VALUES ('#{h}', ...) uses unvalidated free-text old setting values, so any value containing a single quote produces broken SQL and crashes the migration, and blank lines in the old setting insert host: '' rows that can never match anything.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The interpolated `h` comes from the old `site_settings` value (`val.split("\n")`), which is free-text admin-configurable. If any line contains a single quote, the SQL becomes invalid and can crash the migration (and it is also unsafe SQL construction). Additionally, `split("\n")` will include blank lines as `""`, and the code does not filter them, so it can insert rows with `host = ''` even though such hosts can never match and would violate the model’s format validation (though migrations bypass validations).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb received the old category_fabricator.rb content (all four :category fabricators) while spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines :embeddable_host; it only works because Fabrication loads by glob rather than filename, so anyone later editing the category fabricator edits the wrong file.

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController returns 500s instead of 404/422 on missing records/params: update/destroy do where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call methods on the result, so a stale id yields nil.host= / nil.destroy and a NoMethodError; params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises if the envelope is absent; and a nil host reaches before_validation where nil.sub! raises instead of producing a validation error.

Admin::EmbeddingController#update accepts a PUT and persists nothing: the action ignores the request body and just re-serializes, while the JS saveChanges action calls embedding.update({}); nothing in embedding.hbs invokes saveChanges today, but any future save button wired to it would silently discard user input while returning HTTP 200.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is wired to `put "customize/embedding"` but the action does not read params or persist anything; it just re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). On the client, `admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but `embedding.hbs` currently has no save button invoking it, and all actual mutations (hosts) are persisted via `EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save(props)` / `destroyRecord`). So this is a real, diff-grounded concern about a misleading/placeholder PUT endpoint and unused save action, but not a currently user-visible defect in the shown UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: delete() in admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 swallows destroyRecord failures: destroyRecord().then(...) has no .catch, so if the DELETE fails the confirm dialog closes, the row remains, and no error is surfaced (unhandled rejection), unlike save() which correctly uses popupAjaxError.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete() action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch handler. If the DELETE request fails, the rejection is unhandled and no error UI is shown (unlike save(), which does .catch(popupAjaxError)); the row also won’t be removed because deleteHost is only sent in the success callback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host validation vs. lookup mismatch on ports: the format regex in app/models/embeddable_host.rb explicitly permits a port ((:[0-9]{1,5})?), but record_for_host compares against uri.host which never includes a port, so a saved example.com:3000 authorizes nothing even though port-bearing entries worked under the old URI-parsed setting.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, the validation regex allows an optional port (":[0-9]{1,5}") and the before_validation callback strips scheme and path but does not strip a port, so a record can be saved as "example.com:3000". However, record_for_host(url) parses the incoming URL and matches using uri.host (host only, no port) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored host containing a port will never match and thus `host_allowed?` will reject it. This is a verifiable mismatch/regression introduced by the new model-based allowlist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host format regex requires a TLD (\.[a-z]{2,5}), so TLD-less hosts like localhost or intranet names — accepted by the old free-text setting — can no longer be created or re-saved through the UI.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host` with `/\A...\.[a-z]{2,5}...\Z/i`, which requires a dot + 2–5 letter TLD (e.g. `example.com`). This excludes TLD-less hosts like `localhost` or intranet names. Since the admin UI now creates/updates hosts via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` -> `host.save`, such hosts cannot be created or re-saved if present. The old setting-based approach (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` + `allows_embeddable_host?`) did not impose this regex constraint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch in discourse/models/store.js.es6 crashes on any non-array *_ids value: now every key matching /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ is processed and obj[k].map(...) assumes an array, so a payload emitting foo_ids: null or a scalar throws inside shared hydration code, breaking find/findAll for that type entirely; also hydrated || [] is dead code and failed lookups insert nulls into the hydrated list.

adjudication.rationale: In discourse/models/store.js.es6, _hydrateEmbedded now matches both *_id and *_ids via /(.+)\_id(s?)$/. When the key is plural (m[2] truthy), it unconditionally executes obj[k].map(...). If a payload provides a non-array value for foo_ids (e.g., null or a scalar), this will throw at runtime and break hydration for that record/type. Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead because `.map` always returns an array if reached, and failed lookups can yield undefined entries that are inserted into the resulting list without filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post-save client state diverges from the server in admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6: the buffer is never rolled back after a successful save, so re-editing shows the pre-normalization input (e.g. http://foo.com) while the row displays the server-normalized foo.com; and when the category chooser is cleared, the server saves uncategorized_category_id but the client sets category to findById(null) (undefined), so the badge renders blank until reload.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the template binds the edit input to `buffered.host` (`{{input value=buffered.host ...}}`). On successful `save()`, the code only toggles `editToggled` false and never calls `rollbackBuffer()` / otherwise re-syncs the buffer (`host.save(props).then(() => { ... this.set('editToggled', false); })`). Since the server normalizes `host` in `EmbeddableHost` `before_validation` (strips scheme/path), the row can display normalized `host.host` while the buffer can still contain the pre-normalized string when re-editing. Also, when `categoryId` is cleared, the client sends `category_id = null`, but the server sets it to `uncategorized_category_id` (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`). After save, the client forcibly sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which with `null` yields `undefined`, so `{{category-badge host.category}}` can render blank until reload, even though the server stored uncategorized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: host.isSaving may not exist on RestModel: if RestModel (unlike Ember Data) does not define isSaving, the cantSave guard and the disabled=host.isSaving bindings are permanently falsy, and a double-click during a slow save issues two POSTs, creating duplicate host rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `cantSave` and template bindings depending on `host.isSaving` (`admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` and `templates/components/embeddable-host.hbs`), but it does not include the `RestModel` implementation (or any model definition for `embeddable-host`) to verify whether `isSaving` exists/gets set during `host.save(...)`. The claim that `isSaving` is missing and therefore double-clicking will issue two POSTs is speculative and not verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store test asserts the wrong record: the pretender's /fruits/:id handler returns fruits[0], so store.find('fruit', 2) is served fruit 1 (apple), and the new plural-hydration assertions (colors length 2, ids 1 and 2) validate apple's color_ids rather than banana's [3]; the test passes for the wrong record and would not catch a lookup regression on the actually-requested record.

adjudication.rationale: In test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6 the Pretender handler for `this.get('/fruits/:id', ...)` ignores `request.params.id` and always returns `const fruit = fruits[0];` (apple, id 1, `color_ids: [1,2]`). The updated store test in test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6 calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` has length 2 with ids 1 and 2—assertions that only match apple, not the requested banana (id 2, `color_ids: [3]`). Therefore the test passes while validating the wrong record and would not catch regressions in id-based lookup/hydration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed hot path performance regression: `ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, issuing a DB query (`WHERE lower(host) = ?`) on every `/embed/comments` request, replacing the process-cached `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` which required zero DB traffic; the host list should be cached (process/Redis, invalidated on host CRUD) instead of queried per request

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` to `raise ... unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), i.e., a DB query per `/embed/comments` request. Previously, `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` used the process-cached SiteSetting string and did not require DB access (method removed in app/models/site_setting.rb). This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No functional index on `embeddable_hosts (lower(host))`: the table is created with only a PK, so the hot-path lookup `WHERE lower(host) = ?` cannot use a plain index and requires a sequential scan per embed request

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with only columns (no index on `host` or `lower(host)`). The hot-path lookup in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which cannot use a plain index even if one existed; with no index at all it will require a sequential scan as the table grows. This is a concrete performance/scalability issue introduced by the new table and query, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded materialization in admin embedding endpoints: `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` loads and serializes every host row with no limit/pagination on every `show` and `update`; `update` additionally re-runs the full fetch+serialize while persisting nothing (frontend PUTs empty props)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an unbounded load/serialize of all embeddable hosts in `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` via `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` (used for both `show` and `update` through the `before_filter`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/scalability concern (no pagination/limit) but it does not necessarily constitute a correctness defect given the endpoint is admin-only and intended to list hosts. The finding about `update` persisting nothing is also supported: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` just re-renders the same serialized OpenStruct and the frontend calls `embedding.update({})` with empty props, suggesting the PUT is effectively a refresh/no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsafe SQL interpolation in migration: the INSERT at line 24 of `create_embeddable_hosts.rb` interpolates `#{h}` into raw SQL, so a quote character in a legacy host line breaks the migration

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration loops over legacy `embeddable_hosts` lines and does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration `create_embeddable_hosts` crashes with NoMethodError on any install where the `embed_category` setting was never changed from its default (no `site_settings` row exists), because `execute(...)[0]` returns nil and `nil['id']` is dereferenced — blocking every standard upgrade; masked in CI because test DBs are prepared from schema.rb so the data migration never runs

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when selecting the category from `site_settings` for `embed_category`. If there is no matching row (e.g., the setting was never persisted, so the query returns 0 rows), then `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError`, preventing the migration from running. The later `if category_id == 0` fallback cannot execute because the exception happens first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies embeddable host setting values verbatim via raw SQL without normalizing protocol/path (bypassing the model's `before_validation` stripping), so migrated rows like `http://discourse.org` or `example.com/1234` can never match the new exact `lower(host) = uri.host` lookup, silently breaking existing embeds and causing TopicRetriever to reject feeds after upgrade

`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` update/destroy raise 500 (NoMethodError) instead of 404 for unknown ids because `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil which is then dereferenced via `nil.host=`/`nil.destroy`
`save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without a presence check, causing a 500 on any request that omits the wrapper param

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly accesses `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`). If a client sends a malformed request (or wrong content-type/body) that omits the `embeddable_host` wrapper key, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil[:host]`, resulting in a 500 instead of a handled 4xx error.

Store.js `_hydrateEmbedded` plural branch unconditionally deletes and replaces any payload attribute matching `*_ids` for every model, silently stripping non-association attributes ending in `_ids` from hydrated records, with no audit of other payloads shipping `*_ids` keys

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch matches any key ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, when plural, always assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = ...` and then `delete obj[k];` (the original `*_ids` key) without checking whether that field was intended as an association vs. a plain attribute. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change that could silently drop legitimate non-association `*_ids` attributes in any hydrated payload, but the diff doesn’t prove an existing payload is actually broken by it (the added tests/pretender use `color_ids` as an association).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js plural hydration `obj[k].map(...)` throws TypeError if the `*_ids` value is null, a failure mode the singular branch did not have

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new plural hydration branch assumes `obj[k]` is an array and unconditionally calls `obj[k].map(...)` when the key matches `*_ids` (`if (m[2]) { ... }`). If an API payload includes an `*_ids` field that is `null` (or otherwise not an array), this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime. The previous singular `*_id` branch did not introduce this specific failure mode because it passed the value through `_lookupSubType` without calling array methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js plural hydration failed lookups produce arrays containing null entries (the `hydrated || []` fallback never applies since arrays are truthy), whereas the singular path preserved the raw id on failure

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new plural hydration branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) always constructs `hydrated` as an Array via `obj[k].map(...)`, so `hydrated || []` is ineffective because arrays are always truthy. If `_lookupSubType(...)` fails for an id, the resulting array will contain `undefined`/`null` entries. Additionally, unlike the singular branch (which only deletes `obj[k]` when hydration succeeds), the plural branch unconditionally does `delete obj[k]`, losing the original raw id list even when lookups fail. This matches the finding and is a behavior change/defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHost` format validation advertises `host:port` support (regex permits `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but `record_for_host` compares against `URI(referer).host` which excludes the port, so a stored `example.com:3000` can never match and embeds from that host silently fail authorization

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex permits an optional `:port` (e.g. `example.com:3000`). However `record_for_host` parses the referer via `URI(host)` and uses `uri.host` (hostname only, no port) and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Since `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, a stored value like `example.com:3000` will never equal `uri.host` (`example.com`), so `host_allowed?` can incorrectly deny a valid referer with port and break embedding authorization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` update action re-renders `@embedding` without reading `params` at all, silently discarding any request body and returning 200 with no change — a no-op published API route

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists anything, so `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` is a no-op that returns success regardless of request body. This route is wired in `config/routes.rb` and the Ember controller has an action calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, implying an update endpoint that currently cannot apply changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, `SiteSetting.embed_category`, and the class method `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` are removed outright with no deprecation path or alias, causing unknown-setting/NoMethodError failures for external consumers such as provisioning scripts, admin settings API clients, and plugins

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` method from `app/models/site_setting.rb`, deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` settings from `config/site_settings.yml`, and even deletes those rows in the migration (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). All internal references in this diff are updated to use `EmbeddableHost` instead, so it’s not an app-internal runtime defect. However, the finding’s compatibility concern is diff-grounded: any external code (plugins, scripts, API clients) still calling `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` or expecting those settings to exist would now fail with `NoMethodError`/unknown-setting, and no alias/deprecation shim is provided in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category lookup returns no rows: execute(...)[0] returns nil and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate on fresh installs and sites that never set embed_category; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable and would itself crash pre-seed

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when looking up `embed_category`. If the SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` was never set), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` and aborts `db:migrate`. The subsequent `if category_id == 0` fallback would not be reached because the exception occurs earlier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies old host values verbatim via raw INSERT, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so protocol-prefixed entries like http://discourse.org silently stop matching any referer after upgrade, causing the embed endpoint to reject previously-working hosts with InvalidAccess

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old SiteSetting 'embeddable_hosts' value and does a raw SQL INSERT of each line as the `host` column (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)) without running the EmbeddableHost model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). After the change, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` / `host_allowed?` which compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` (hostname only). If a previously-working entry was stored as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (explicitly supported by the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? implementation that parsed URIs), it would be migrated verbatim and then fail to match `uri.host`, causing embeds to be rejected with InvalidAccess.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update/destroy in admin/embeddable_hosts_controller crash with a 500 on a stale or missing host id: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil and is then used without a nil guard, reachable from the normal UI via concurrent edits or a double-click on delete

If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same issue: update/destroy fetch an EmbeddableHost by id using `where(...).first` which may return nil, and then methods are called on it without checking, causing a 500/NoMethodError when the record is missing or stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client delete path in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch on destroyRecord(), so failed DELETE requests (network blip, 500, session expiry) reject unhandled with no message shown and the row stays in the table
